Share SOC2 + KMS integration checklist and SSO SAML notes

Evan: Run a quick simulation using customer payload distributions and share results by 2025-12-22
Jamal: Provide sample session traces and token distributions by 2025-12-20

meeting_header: Date: 2025-12-18, Start: 15:30 PST, Duration: 48 minutes. Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Redwood Product), Dr. Priya Nair (Halo ML), Jamal Turner (Halo Platform), Lina Gomez (Halo Security)
summary: Optimize walkthrough focused on KV/prefix prefetch strategies and a cost model tailored to Halo Biotech's mix of short chat sessions and long-form generation. Demonstrated Console Optimize recommendations, tradeoffs between batching and latency, cache TTL patterns, and fallback routing to smaller model variants when cold. Agreed next steps: pilot benchmark, share cost spreadsheet and security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Priya, Jamal, Lina, good to have you. We'll run through an Optimize-first walkthrough focused on KV and prefix prefetch, then show a cost model tuned to your session mix. We have about 45 minutes.

[00:18] Priya (Halo): Thanks Samira. Quick context — our app has two main flows: short chatbot-ish interactions (~20 tokens responses) but also heavier report generation where users dump a few paragraphs and we run a 1k token completion. So the cost profile is bimodal. We're trying to understand where prefetch and KV caching help most.

[00:39] Evan (Redwood SE): Great, that's actually a textbook case for prefix caching + dynamic batching. Quick question — what's your median prompt prefix length for the chat sessions?

[00:48] Jamal (Halo): Median is 120 tokens raw but effective prompt after templating is about 80 tokens. For the report flow it's usually 750 token prompt plus 1k expected completion.

[01:05] Evan (Redwood SE): Perfect. So two knobs we'll demo: 1) prefix/KV cache for the ~80-token session prefixes, 2) prefetch warming for likely-next prefixes and how that interacts with batching to avoid cold token costs.

[01:20] Samira (Redwood AE): We'll also show the Console Optimize page where we surface the recommendations and expected unit-cost delta. Marta will flag a few product constraints.

[01:30] Marta (Redwood Product): Heads up, when we talk about prefetching we mean controlled prefetch — not blind warming — because you can overrun throughput if you prefetch aggressively. We recommend heuristics tied to session probability and TTLs.

[01:46] Priya (Halo): Can you show me the cost model for mixed workloads? I worry the batching benefits for big jobs won't help the tiny chat ones.

[01:54] Evan (Redwood SE): Absolutely. Switching to the Console — bear with me while I pull the Optimize scenario. (small typing noises) Okay, on screen: the cost-sim has two workload buckets input — chat (60% of requests, avg 20 output tokens) and reports (40% of requests, avg 1000 output tokens). We model prefix hit-rate, batch size distribution, and KV cache hit TTL.

[02:25] Speaker 3: (unlabeled) Sorry, can you repeat the percent split?

[02:30] Priya (Halo): 60/40 chat to report.

[02:33] Evan (Redwood SE): Thanks. So baseline (no caching, sequential) we show per-token cost X. If we enable prefix cache with a 70% hit rate on chat prefixes and TTL of 10 minutes, the chat token cost drops dramatically because we avoid the encoder/attention recompute for that prefix.

[02:55] Jamal (Halo): How are you estimating the hit rate? Our user queries have some variability.

[03:01] Evan (Redwood SE): Good point. There are two ways: empirical from sampled session traces (we can ingest a small trace sample) or synthetic via clustering your prompts. In the Console you can upload a token distribution CSV and we run a clustering + estimated hit partition. We showed a sample clustering earlier.

[03:20] Lina (Halo): On the security side, we need to understand retention and KMS. If you cache prefixes, where do they land? Are they encrypted?

[03:28] Marta (Redwood Product): By default in Hosted, KV cache resides in encrypted Redis with KMS keys managed by Redwood; we also support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. TTLs are configurable and audit logs show cache access events. We'll send the SOC2 excerpt with the KMS flow.

[03:48] Evan (Redwood SE): Back to the cost sim: important nuance — prefix caching helps most on short sessions where encoder cost is a larger fraction. For your long report runs the dominant cost is decoder tokens; batching report jobs yields much more amortization there. So you should use both: prefix cache + moderate batching on chat to preserve SLOs, and higher batch targets for report processing, maybe scheduled windows or background workers.

[04:15] Priya (Halo): And what's the latency impact for chat when you enable cache + batching? We need 200ms p95.

[04:22] Evan (Redwood SE): If you keep batch windows small (100ms micro-batches) and hit-rate is above 50%, p95 stays under 200ms on our Dedicated configs. For Hosted, p95 depends on region and load but Console shows simulated latency distribution.

[04:40] Samira (Redwood AE): Also worth mentioning routing policies — we can pin latency-sensitive routes to Dedicated or reserved pool and route cold or batchy report jobs to cheaper capacity. That gives you cost control without sacrificing p95.

[04:56] Jamal (Halo): How does prefetching work in practice? Is it synchronous when a session starts or async warming?

[05:05] Evan (Redwood SE): Two patterns: 1) On-demand prefix resolution — the moment a session starts we check KV and if miss, we can synchronously warm top-k cached vectors. That adds a small delta (tens of ms). 2) Predictive prefetch — based on telemetry we warm likely prefixes in background ahead of predicted sessions. Predictive warms are good for repeated workflows.

[05:30] Priya (Halo): Any risk of unnecessary cost from predictive warms?

[05:33] Marta (Redwood Product): Yes, if not tuned. That's why Optimize has a prefetch budget and ROI calculator — it recommends max warm-per-hour based on expected hit-rate and cost per warm. Evan, can you pull the ROI panel?

[05:45] Evan (Redwood SE): Pulling it now. See the right-hand side — ROI preview. Example: if a warm costs ~0.002 tokens-equivalent (warm is primarily encoder compute), and it prevents 10 decoder tokens on average, the ROI is high for short sessions. The Console shows estimated net savings and suggests TTL and prefetch thresholds.

[06:12] Speaker 2: (background) mhm

[06:15] Samira (Redwood AE): Quick commercial note — for Dedicated reserved capacity we can price reserved pools differently which makes aggressive prefetching more attractive because marginal warm cost goes down. That's often a lever for customers with stable predictable traffic.

[06:29] Jamal (Halo): We're evaluating hosted first but open to Dedicated if we see steady usage. Could the same config be ported to Private later?

[06:36] Marta (Redwood Product): Yes, same API and optimize profiles. Just KMS and network controls change in Private. We keep the Optimize recommendations consistent so your scripts/ops don't need rework.

[06:52] Priya (Halo): Can you do an example where we tune TTLs for a 60/40 mix?

[06:58] Evan (Redwood SE): Sure: switching TTL slider to 5 minutes — projected chat prefix hit falls to 45% because ephemeral sessions drop out. Cost reduction for chat becomes smaller. If we move TTL to 30 minutes hit jumps to 75% — but you pay more storage. Console computes net token-savings per hour and highlights the sweet spot.

[07:28] Priya (Halo): What's the storage cost per prefix?

[07:32] Evan (Redwood SE): Tiny — we price KV storage per GB-month. In most configs, storage is a rounding error vs inference compute, but for very large prefix catalogs you'd want to use eviction heuristics.

[07:45] Jamal (Halo): About the fallback policy — if cache miss and Dedicated isn't available, can we fallback to a smaller model automatically?

[07:53] Evan (Redwood SE): Yes, smart routing can fall back to compatible model variants. You set policy: prefer latency or prefer cost. We demo a canary policy in the Console.

[08:06] Priya (Halo): I'm worried about hallucination/regression when using smaller models for fallback. Any guardrails?

[08:12] Marta (Redwood Product): Validate via evals — Optimize ties into our evals feature. You can create prompt sets and run automatic quality regressions. If fallback causes quality drop beyond threshold, we block the route or alert you.

[08:28] Samira (Redwood AE): Ok Evan let's switch to a concrete example — I want you to make a copy of their token distribution and run two scenarios: one with prefix cache + small batching on chat, and one without cache but larger batching across both flows.

[08:45] Evan (Redwood SE): Doing that. (typing) Scenario A: cache enabled, chat batch window 100ms, report batch window 500ms. Scenario B: no cache, global batching window 300ms. Simulation results populating...

[09:05] Evan (Redwood SE): Results: Scenario A projected monthly cost $16.2k for the assumed volume; Scenario B projected $21.7k. Biggest delta comes from chat where prefix cache saved ~45% of compute for that bucket. However, report latency in Scenario B improved by 15ms due to bigger batches.

[09:30] Priya (Halo): Those dollar values are helpful — can we get them exported to CSV for our finance team?

[09:36] Samira (Redwood AE): Yes we'll export and send — action item.

[09:42] Jamal (Halo): How accurate are these sims vs real run? Our traffic bursts and cold-starts worry me.

[09:48] Evan (Redwood SE): Simming accuracy depends on the fidelity of input distributions. If you provide sample session traces we'll run a bench to validate. Typically sims are within 10-15% if the sample is representative.

[10:02] Priya (Halo): Let's talk about implementation complexity — what code changes on our side for prefix caching + prefetch?

[10:10] Evan (Redwood SE): Minimal. On the client side you need a small SDK call to check and insert into KV (we have SDKs in Python/Node). Prefetch can be implemented as a background worker or integrated into your session orchestrator. We'll share a quickstart repo.

[10:24] Samira (Redwood AE): We'll attach a sample patch showing where to call the SDK, TTL patterns, and a prefetch example.

[10:30] Lina (Halo): From security: does the SDK send full prompts to Redwood for prefetch decisions? We need to scrub PHI.

[10:36] Marta (Redwood Product): You can hash prefixes client-side and use hashed keys for cache lookup; Optimize accepts hashed traces for hit-rate estimation. For PHI we'd recommend on-prem Private deployment or token scrubbing prior to upload. We'll include guidance in the security doc.

[10:56] Priya (Halo): Good. What's the expected timeline for a pilot?

[11:00] Samira (Redwood AE): If you send traces by Friday, Evan can run a bench next week and we can stand up a 2-week pilot the following week.

[11:08] Jamal (Halo): Sounds reasonable. Regarding pricing, can you show dedicated reserved example?

[11:12] Samira (Redwood AE): We'll send the reserved example in the pricing doc. High level: reserved pools reduce per-token cost for steady throughput and make aggressive prefetch warm budgets cheaper.

[11:22] Priya (Halo): Any regulatory note for EU users? We have EU research groups with data residency needs.

[11:28] Marta (Redwood Product): We have EU-hosted regions and Private deploy options for strict residency. We'll send the region availability matrix.

[11:36] Evan (Redwood SE): One more demo note: On Console we can simulate different TTL eviction policies — LRU vs LFU vs frequency + recency hybrid. For your use-case with many ephemeral prefixes, hybrid LFU+TTL often performs best.

[11:54] Jamal (Halo): Can you include the sample LRU vs LFU sim in the exported CSV?

[11:58] Evan (Redwood SE): Yes. We'll include both sims and the per-bucket delta.

[12:04] Priya (Halo): Onboarding ask — will you need infra access for the pilot? We prefer not to give credentials.

[12:10] Samira (Redwood AE): No credentials required for the initial sim; for pilot we provide a one-time signed ingest token and you control the dataset upload. For Private we'd do a network onboarding checklist.

[12:22] Lina (Halo): Okay please send the KMS and retention notes. Also need to confirm audit log format.

[12:28] Marta (Redwood Product): We'll attach a sample audit log and KMS integration diagram.

[12:36] Samira (Redwood AE): To recap next steps: we'll send pricing/reserved examples, the cost-simulation CSV, security docs, and a quickstart patch. Evan will run the deeper bench when Jamal provides traces.

[12:53] Priya (Halo): Great. One last question — do you have any built-in alerts for cache churn or when prefetch ROI drops?

[12:59] Evan (Redwood SE): Yes, Optimize has alerting: hit-rate drop, prefetch budget exhaustion, and unusual TTL churn. Alerts can be routed to Slack or to your webhook.

[13:12] Jamal (Halo): Perfect. We'll get traces over by Friday. Thanks everyone.

[13:18] Samira (Redwood AE): Thanks all. We'll follow up with the files and calendar invite for the pilot kick-off.

[13:26] (call ends)
